Laura / Rishi — forwarding ClearWave's annotated redline. Procurement wants a clear reply by EOD Thursday. Can you review and recommend exact wording we can propose in the MSA & Order Form? Customer preference is ownership + opt-out but we should offer a fallback.

Below are the scenarios I'd like proposed language for (bullet points are for legal drafting — please keep short):

1) Customer ownership carveout (customer-owned outputs): short clause that assigns ownership of "Customer Outputs" to ClearWave when such outputs are generated solely from data submitted by the customer and not from Redwood-proprietary prompts or templates. Consider a definition: "Customer Outputs: text, code, or other content generated by the Service that is derived solely from Customer Content and Customer Prompts."

2) Training opt-out (order form checkbox): one-line option that if checked, Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs for model training or to improve models and will exclude such data from training pipelines for the duration of the contract + 180 days post-termination. Include an exception for aggregated telemetry (latency/error rates) that is irreversibly aggregated and not linkable to ClearWave.

3) Balanced alternative: Redwood keeps rights to improve models using de-identified, aggregated signals but agrees to implement a data exclusion flag at the tenant level for any raw input/output pairs that ClearWave marks as excluded.

Please attach suggested text snippets and flag any operational blockers (e.g., hosted customers can't get full opt-out without environment isolation). Also alert if this triggers a pricing/discount discussion (it might).

Thanks — Hannah

Maria — thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround. We discussed internally and have three concrete, mutually exclusive options below. Please let us know which you prefer and we'll update the MSA + Order Form and circulate for signature.

Option A — Customer Ownership + Training Exclusion (Conservative) - "Customer Outputs" are owned by the Customer. "Customer Outputs" means content generated by the Service that is derived solely from Customer Content and Customer Prompts. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs for model training, tuning, or weight updates. Tenant-level exclusion will be implemented for the contract term plus 180 days after termination. Aggregated, irreversible telemetry (e.g., latency percentiles, system error rates) may be used for service reliability and capacity planning only.

Option B — Service Improvement License with Identifiability Exclusion (Balanced) - Redwood retains the right to use de-identified and aggregated signals (including input/output pairs where ClearWave-identifiers are removed) to improve model quality, provided that ClearWave can mark specific input/output pairs or data sources for exclusion at the tenant level. Redwood will not use any data that ClearWave has flagged as excluded for model training.

Option C — Redwood Default (Standard) with Customer Commitments (Standard) - Redwood retains rights to use inputs/outputs to improve models (standard feedback license) but commits to additional operational safeguards for ClearWave, including enhanced access logging, per-token telemetry filtered by tenant, and a quarterly review of any model-level drift. This option carries no change to model IP assignment (outputs remain under Redwood license to operate the service).

Practical notes:
- For hosted customers, Option A requires isolation and is typically sold with Dedicated or Private (we can provide a price add for the exclusion).
- Option B is often acceptable for mid-enterprise deals: it balances ClearWave's need to avoid direct retraining on their data while allowing us to improve models in aggregate.
- Option C is the fastest to sign; Options A/B will impact pricing and may need procurement approval.

Next steps:
1) Tell us preferred option by EOD Thursday and I will issue a clean MSA + Order Form with chosen language.
2) If Option A is selected, our sales ops team will prepare a cost addendum for the tenant-level exclusion.
3) We can join a short legal-to-legal call if ClearWave legal wants to walk through the clauses.

Copying Laura & Rishi for any final edits to the draft language before we send the clean docs.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
